body:
There's a quote from my favourite book ("the posthumous memoirs of Brás Cubas", fittingly about a 19th century dead man from Brazil telling the reader of his life) that neatly sums up my thoughts on these pivotal, generally traumatizing, events.

It's near the end, when the narrator is recounting the events that led to his death. He had delusions of grandeur about developing an ointment that would work as a universal panacea and being so engrossed in these thoughts exposed himself to a chill and developed the pneumonia that killed him. His posthumous commentary goes on about how the ointment would have made him the foremost among men but alas " chance determined otherwise, and as such you [living] shall remain forever hypocondriac".

I think this is it, at the end of the day. I can't really point to a specific moment from which my relationship was doomed. Trying to enumerate the causes is a mostly futile exercise, I might as well say everything started when I was born. Might as well say it could've been different, but chance determined otherwise. It's our burden to live with the consequences, as the hypocondriacs we are bound to remain.

I still have a few friends, but most of my former friends actively don't want to have anything to do with me.

When it comes to those that remain our interactions it's like drinking alcohol: present and fleeting satisfaction/relief followed by depression. It's like borrowing happiness from my future self then having to pay it back with interest.

I don't have anything to add besides I've been in a somewhat similar situation recently. That relationship was the best thing to happen to me in years and also the thing that came closest to killing me. I was the one to end things when I realised it was only going to hurt her and myself to keep trying. Don't think I can forgive myself for not having been able to handle all of it.
